chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The divorce of a pregnant woman is one (irrevocable pronouncement), and her waiting period is until she delivers her pregnancy. So when she delivers what is in her womb, she has been separated from him.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She has been separated from him

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a pregnant woman after divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific iddah of a pregnant woman, establishing that her waiting period concludes upon parturition rather than the completion of three menstrual cycles. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the finality of divorce and the eligibility for remarriage, emphasizing the physical reality of childbirth as the definitive marker of the iddah period.
